cases.answer: In Jan et al.'s Table 4 (allelic frequencies in 200 sulphonylurea-induced-hypoglycaemia cases vs 200 controls in a Pakistani Pashtun T2DM population), the CYP2C9*2 line ('Decreases enzyme activity') prints: cases 35 (17.5%), controls 12 (6.0%), OR 0.102 (95% CI 0.08–3.08), crude p = 0.021, adjusted p = 0.031. This line cannot be treated as an internally coherent risk estimate, for three reasons visible in the article itself. First, the direction is wrong: an OR of 0.102 (<1) implies a protective allele, yet the same table and text show the allele enriched in cases (17.5% vs 6.0%) and the discussion calls it a higher carriage in cases; an OR computed from the printed counts would be roughly 3.3, not 0.102. Second, the 95% CI 0.08–3.08 spans 1, which is incompatible with the printed significant p-values (0.021 crude, 0.031 adjusted). Third, the table's own title mislabels the variants as 'CYPC19*2 and CYPC19*3' instead of CYP2C9. The discussion repeats the incoherent OR = 0.102 with p = 0.021, so the error is not just a single table typo.

cases.answer: Dabbs-Brown et al. (PLoS Genetics 2025) examined sex-stratified interactions between a type 2 diabetes polygenic risk score (PRST2D) and sex hormones in white European UK Biobank participants, excluding individuals with type 1 diabetes. The strongest interaction was PRST2D-by-SHBG in women: interaction OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85–0.90. The p-value is printed as P = 1.09E-18 in the abstract and in Table 2, and as p < 2 × 10-16 in the results text. The female SHBG model comprised 12,502 T2D cases and 181,955 controls (Table 2; the SHBG sub-cohort overall included 194,833 women). An interaction OR below 1 means the PRS-associated odds of T2D are attenuated at higher SHBG levels; it was the most significant of the six PRS-by-hormone interaction models tested.

cases.answer: The premise is wrong: the original Berthoumieux digital DSMES+CGM randomized cohort had no twelve-month measurement. The trial (adults with type 2 diabetes, baseline HbA1c >= 8%, n=51 digital DSMES+CGM vs n=49 usual care) ran for 6 months, with HbA1c assessed at 3 and 6 months as the primary outcome. The HbA1c difference versus usual care was −0.7% (95% CI −1.4% to −0.1%; −8.1 mmol/mol, 95% CI −15.5 to −0.7; P=.03) at 3 months and −0.6% (95% CI −1.4% to 0.2%; −6.9 mmol/mol, 95% CI −15.7 to 1.9; P=.12) at 6 months — the latest time point reported. The only '12 months' in the article is an exclusion criterion (life expectancy <12 months), not a follow-up point.
